title: From proof generation to mathematical ecosystems
question: When proofs become cheap to produce, who—or what—decides which work should be verified, understood, reused, or pursued?
body: As formal proof production becomes more abundant, correctness remains necessary but may no longer be the hardest bottleneck. Mathematical context, understanding, value, transfer, and reuse may become equally important.

title: From agent coordination to evolving organizations
question: When many agents share a difficult task, how can the system discover and revise its communities, routes, protocols, and resource allocation?
body: As the number of agents grows, the central problem may move beyond assigning tasks. Organization, information flow, communication, and the division between local and global decisions may themselves become objects of experiment.

title: Scaling evidence and state
question: How can a system preserve enough structure, provenance, and feedback for work to remain checkable and useful as tasks, agents, and artifacts multiply?
body: This is the bridge between the two horizons and the projects already recorded here: local reasoning only becomes cumulative when a system can retain, evaluate, and organize what happened.
